balls.text: slower ball down the leg side and Binny opens up and swings it away over the backward square leg boundary
shot. It's very full on middle stump, not quite a yorker, and that's enough of an error in length as Binny makes room and carves it through square cover
very full on off stump, swiped down to long-on
full-toss on middle stump, and that's a super shot from Samson, clears his front leg and bisects long on and deep midwicket
off-stump yorker, carved away without any great timing, into the covers
and he strikes. Very full on middle and leg. Nair looks to hoick it away over the leg side, doesn't really get hold of it, picks out Axar at deep square leg
very full, follows Nair who was backing away from the stumps. Looked to whip it into the leg side and it hit his pads and ricocheted towards short third man
middle-stump yorker, dug out towards point
another slower ball, was it? Full outside leg stump and he looked to sweep it over short fine leg. Too early into his shot and it bounced off the back of his bat towards short third man
good slower ball, angled across Karun. He looked to make room to crash it through the covers, and came nowhere near connecting as it kept low and dribbled through to the keeper
full-toss and Nair clears his front leg and Javed Miandads it over the square leg boundary. Poor ball, that.

got him! That was cleanly struck by Faulkner, clearing his front leg and hitting the full middle-stump ball down the ground, but didn't get enough elevation to clear long-on. Maxwell timed his jump perfectly to catch it two-handed, over his head
looks for the full slower ball, slips it down the leg side
full outside off, lofted to the left of long-off
full-toss on off stump, punched down to long-off
greets Faulkner with a high full-toss very wide outside off. It was a good-length ball if Saha had been batting
slower ball slanting away from off stump, and Saha takes a good low catch to his right, after Rahane looked to slog it over the leg side and only managed a top-edge
slower ball, full on middle stump. Rahane shuffled across, waited for it to come on, and clipped it elegantly over the square leg umpire. Top shot.
low full-toss close to off stump, chipped in the air, one bounce to Marsh at long-off
low full-toss outside off, shovelled firmly towards long-on, lots of bottom hand
starts with the bouncer, and it definitely bounced over Nair's head, given wide. He stood there, and checked himself from hooking
down the track now, whips away the leg-stump ball towards deep backward square leg
very full on middle stump, clears his front leg and whips it towards deep midwicket
the conventional square sweep now. This was tossed up a bit more and he hits it to the right of deep midwicket, picks up two

another reverse-sweep, and this time he played it almost on the half-volley. So close to his foot Shivam appealed for lbw, but he middled it and sent it screaming to the boundary to the left of short fine leg
full-toss on leg stump, and Nair calmly reverse-paddles it to the left of short fine leg
full on middle and leg, clipped to the right of deep midwicket
shot! Sees a bit of air outside off and gets down nice and low to get the elevation to launch it over cover
back of a length on off stump, back and across to work it to long-on
very full and wide. Rahane stretches out to slice it towards point
out first ball! It was a long-hop, or a longish-hop at any rate, and Smith pulls it straight down the throat of deep midwicket
down the track again, looks to slog this off-stumpish ball across the line, inside-edges into his pad and it ricochets into the off side
down the track, checked drive towards cover
bowled him, or is that bowled himself? Stretched across the stumps a long way to play the lap sweep to the full ball on leg stump, didn't make any contact
full-toss on middle stump, whipped to midwicket
shot! This is superb from Hooda, who clears his front leg to this full ball on the stumps and drives with a free swing of his bat to pierce the gap between long-on and deep midwicket
full on leg stump, driven to mid-on
down the track now. Shivam sees him coming and bowls it flat and wide outside off, and Rahane simply swishes his bat through the line to launch it over the cover boundary
fullish on middle stump, and Rahane clears his front leg and swipes it away to the left of deep square leg
low full-toss outside off, whipped to midwicket
back of a length outside off, tried to flat-bat it through the off side, didn't come on, hit it straight back towards the bowler
shortish on off stump. Hooda rides the bounce and defends with soft hands into the leg side
yorker on off stump, dug out towards deep point

length ball outside off, and that's Rahane's first six, a pick-up shot whipped to the right of deep midwicket, not too far out of his reach. Sandeep leaped diagonally but couldn't get his hand to it, and Rahane brings up his fifty
low full-toss on off stump, punched back firmly to the bowler
sees Hooda make room and fires it full and wide, but to no avail. Hooda gets down low again, and launches it high and clean over long-on
down the track, Maxwell floats it at his feet, and he clips it gently through the vacant mid-on region. Maxwell chases back to field it
fuller and flatter on the pads, clipped away towards deep square leg
wow. Saw a bit of air outside off, and got down on one knee and sent it soaring over wide long-on with a huge, free swing of his arms
fired in full and flat on middle and off, Hooda jams down on it, stabs it back to the bowler
length ball, angling towards Rahane's pads, flicked to deep square leg
back of a length, angling into leg stump. Rahane went down almost on one knee to pull it, and nearly popped a catch to short fine leg. Fell just short of him as he dived forward
tossed up outside off, driven to the right of sweeper cover
a bit of flight, angled in towards middle stump, clipped to deep midwicket

gone! Saw Watson stepping down the pitch and fired in an arm ball that slid between bat and pad, and Saha did brilliantly there, in such an understated way, to collect calmly outside leg stump and whip off the bails
full on leg stump, cramping Watson who's backing away to make room. Defends into the covers
fullish on off stump, whipped with the angle towards deep midwicket
slower ball, full and angling into off stump. Watson defends towards point

slower ball angling across towards off stump. Rahane comes forward, lets it come on, and dabs it away towards point. Direct hit at the batsman's end as they take the single, Maxwell is the fielder, and they go to the third umpire but Watson was easily home
full on off stump, driven to long-off. Good over here, bowling to his field
another full slower ball, on off stump this time, driven firmly to long-off
another slower ball, slanted full and wide outside off. Rahane reaches out to try and drive, can't connect
slower ball outside off, cracked away to deep point
back of a length outside off, Rahane skips back and opens his bat face to punch it to the left of sweeper cover
good ball. Saw Watson making room and followed him with the arm ball. Jammed his bat down to stab it towards backward point
a bit slower now and Watson loves that. Makes room for himself, gets down low, and lofts it high over long-off
full outside off, Rahane eases the drive to the left of sweeper cover
full, speared into leg stump. Rahane can't get the flick away, rolls off the pad to the right of short midwicket
length ball, angled into the pads, tucked away between deep square leg and deep midwicket
full on middle stump, and again Watson gives long-on no chance, hitting hard and ramrod-straight
full-toss on off stump, and Anureet misfields a fairly simple stop at midwicket, low to his right, and concedes another boundary
tossed up again, on a perfect hitting length outside off, and Watson mows it away over the wide long-on boundary, hitting cleanly, with the turn
tossed up full on middle stump, and Watson drives that so powerfully and so straight that neither long-on nor long-off, converging on the ball, can't stop it
length ball outside off. Rahane stays back again and whips it with the turn towards long-on
fullish ball on off stump. Rahane stays on the back foot and defends into the covers
full, a bit of outswing outside off, and Watson gets a move on with a thick edge to the third man boundary. He was making room, looking to launch it over cover
full outside off, didn't come on as quickly as Rahane expected. He wanted to drive through cover, and the bottom hand came into it and he ended up hitting it towards long-off
length ball close to off stump. Again Watson makes a lot of room and wallops it straight to sweeper cover

again Rahane is struck on the pad trying to work the ball across the line. Bounces away into the off side. Not much of an appeal, and he looked to have shuffled across enough to be struck outside the line
length ball on off stump. Watson backed away from the stumps even before Anureet had reached the bowling crease, and slapped it away to the sweeper cover fielder
length ball outside off, whipped wristily to long-on
shortish ball fired into middle stump. Rahane crouches low to be able to pull that towards deep square leg
back of a length on a fourth-stump line. Rahane makes room to cut, can't beat point
a bit of flight now, on off stump, driven to long-off
again he angles it into the pads, and Rahane comes on the front foot to knock it away towards fine leg
short, down the leg side, ricochets off Saha's gloves and rolls away into the leg side. He must have been unsighted by Watson's attempted pull
angles this into the pads, Rahane clips it away towards fine leg
back of a length, angling in towards off stump. Watson makes room and slaps it to sweeper cover
wow. That wasn't the greatest ball, lots of width, but such a crisp sound when Rahane cracked that to the square cover boundary. Bent at the knees to get down low and simply flat-batted it away
shot! That was a length ball on leg stump, and Rahane cleared his front leg and whipped it away over square leg
back of a length outside off. Watson waits on it and steers it to the right of third man
full ball on off stump, too full to drive with power, gives mid-off enough time to move to his right and cut it off easily
shortish ball climbing towards Watson's ribcage. Opens up, jumps to get on top of the bounce, and defends into the on side
length ball on middle and leg. Watson defends to short midwicket
back of a length, curving into the pads, tucked away to short fine leg
length ball, swinging into the pads, flicked straight to short fine leg
full this time, swings in again. Watson wants to drive through cover initially, and ends up hitting it back towards the bowler, didn't hit anywhere near the sweet spot
this time he can't control the line of the inswinger, sends it swerving down the leg side
another inswinger just short of a good length, tucking Watson up for room. Ends up punching it back to the bowler
back of a length on off stump, a bit of inswing. Watson looks to punch it through cover, inside-edges it to the right of short midwicket
another inswinger, and Rahane is hit on the pad again, trying to work it across the line. Ball was sliding down leg, and it rolls away through backward square leg
on the pads now and Rahane clips it to the long leg fielder

length ball on a fourth-stump line, and Sehwag applauds heartily, because Rahane played a super shot there. Stayed next to the line and crashed it away, almost a front-foot cut, to the point boundary. Shades of Dravid in that shot

here's the bouncer, and Rahane isn't in a great position to pull. Top-edges it and it goes high in the air and bounces into the long leg boundary, to the right of the fielder there, who is stationed quite square, almost at deep backward square leg
and again some inswing, and again it hits Rahane's thrust-across front pad. He plays all around it again and gets a thick inside edge into his pad
excellent delivery, a bit of inswing to rap Rahane on the front pad as he plays across it. Not given. Maybe it pitched outside leg stump a touch, maybe it was a bit high.
starts with a length ball, angled across Rahane. Once again the ball doesn't quite come on for the cover drive, and he drags it into the leg side
full outside off, Watson is too early into the drive, sends it running off the inside half of his bat towards square leg
back of a length, looking to tuck Watson up for room, ends up sliding it down the leg side
length ball outside off, swings away to beat Watson's angled-bat drive away from the body
another fullish outswinger outside off. Rahane is too early into his attempted cover drive, drags it towards mid-on
this time it's full and wide and Rahane comes forward and flat-bats it to the square cover boundary
this one holds its line. Rahane is playing for inswing, looking to flick from outside off, and gets a leading edge that loops over the cover fielder and falls in no man's land
big appeal for lbw as Rahane plays around his front pad to try and flick this inswinger. Nice length, and it hit him in line, but there was an inside-edge on it
back of a length, a bit of movement in towards off and middle. Tucked away through backward square leg
overpitched outside off and Watson comes forward to drive it between cover point and short extra cover. Miller runs back from cover point to pull it back short of the rope
length ball, brings his line much closer to off stump, and Watson pushes it defensively into the covers
once again it's short and wide but this time he cuts it straight to Maxwell
width now, back of a length at a gentle pace, and Watson, who is on the front foot, bends at the knee and crashes it away to the point boundary, screams away to the left of the diving Maxwell
back of a length, a bit of swing in towards off stump. Watson leans back and punches to short cover
length ball on off stump, no swing this time. Watson lets it come on and dabs it away backward of point
length ball outside off, defended towards point

this one goes the other way, but not too much. Starts from a fifth-stump line, on a good length, and Rahane presses forward to push that towards backward point, where Maxwell dives to his left to get a hand to it and slow the ball down
another inswinger on a good length, and this one was headed towards the stumps. Rahane gets his bat down just in time to clip it away towards deep backward square leg
full now, tails in and smacks Watson on the front pad, but it was going down the leg side. Was looking to flick, with his pad thrust across the stumps, and it rolled away through backward square leg
back of a length, a bit of swing in towards middle stump, tucked away towards square leg
he's hit it for four and he's tied it! It's full and wide, and he slices under it and sends it to the deep point boundary, one bounce! We're going to have the Super Over.
down the track, making room, and he slices the low full-toss to the right of sweeper cover, and they take two again. Samson doesn't collect cleanly, makes it easier for Axar, who slides home.
full outside off, gets his front foot across and swipes it to long-on. Smith's throw to the keeper's end is wide of the stumps, and they get the second easily
full-toss close to off stump. Johnson makes room and slaps it to deep cover

full outside off, swiped to the left of long-on. They take on Smith's arm, because they want Johnson on strike, and he goes for the bowler's end, and Samson is quick to get the bails off but Johnson is just about home, at full stretch. Excellent running.
full-toss outside off, swiped down to long-on, and Smith, attacking the ball and swooping down to pick-up and throw, fumbles and lets them get two
back to full and straight. Johnson makes room and drives it down to long-off
another slower ball, on leg stump, and Johnson steps across again and simply helps it into the gap to the left of short fine leg
slower bouncer, ends up bowling it down the leg side. A little unlucky, because he saw Johnson premeditate and shuffle across his stumps
low full-toss on middle and off, smacked down to long-on
another yorker, dug out into the covers

slower ball angled across Johnson, and Rahane makes a great attempt but puts him down. Went for the big swipe down the ground, top-edged it very high, and Rahane had to run in a long way from long-on. Caught it with both hands but it popped out as he fell forward onto the ground
full and straight, digs it out towards long-off
full-toss down the leg side, gets down on one knee and swats it to deep midwicket
full and wide outside off, and Miller gets under it and slices it straight into sweeper cover's hands. Expensive over, but this could be the wicket that turns it Royals' way.
down the track, and again Hooda follows him with the full ball at his feet, and again he simply flicks him for six. Easy. Brings up his half-century off 29 balls.
a bit of flight, very full outside off, driven to sweeper cover
tossed up full on middle and leg, swiped away to deep midwicket
down the track, Hooda follows Miller, fires it into his feet, but he puts it away easily, pick-up shot over deep midwicket
bowled him! That was full and straight, and Saha was trying to be too cute there. Walked across his stumps, looked for the scoop over short fine leg, and it was far too full for that shot
full-toss on off stump, and that's another stunner from Saha. Got under it and shovelled it to the wide long-on boundary
slower ball just outside off. Miller wanted to pull it, ended up flat-batting it to long-off
full outside off, looked like the slower one. Wanted to drive through cover, ended up driving to long-on
and another! This one's short and Saha's very quick to swivel into the pull and beat long leg running desperately to his left

super shot, this, from Saha. It's very full and straight, not too much swinging room, but he stayed fairly deep in his crease and whipped it away with a lot of bottom hand between long on and deep midwicket
short ball, not the slower ball, and Miller dumps this higher and squarer, over forward square leg this time

this time he waited for it. It was on an off stump line and he picked the slower ball, got his front leg out of the way, and swivelled through his hips to swat that over the straight midwicket boundary
another slower ball, another missed pull, and it rolls down to the keeper. Didn't miss off stump by much
back of a length outside off, poked towards point for a quick single

another slower short ball, but Saha stayed nice and still, with a stable base, and pulled it firmly to the right of Binny at deep square leg. He ran to his right and got a hand to it, so I guess that's a drop, but a great effort, and it bounces down and rolls into the rope. Saved two runs, I suppose.
there's another slower short ball from Faulkner, angling into Miller's body and hits him on the hip as he swivels to pull. Bounces away into the off side
sees him come down the track and fires it down the leg side. Miller adjusts his feet and flicks to deep midwicket
loopy full-toss wide of off stump, driven to sweeper cover
down the track, whips the leg-stump ball towards deep square leg

loopy googly, and that's produced the breakthrough. Nice line from Tambe, challenged Marsh to hit him against the turn, and he top-edged the attempted slog-sweep high in the air, drops into the waiting hands of Rahane at long-on
sees him coming and fires it into his feet. Drives it firmly to long-on
length ball on off stump, and Miller makes room to carve it into the gap between long-off and deep cover
down the track, clips this full ball towards short fine leg
full on middle stump, and that is power. Gets his front leg out of the way and flat-bats it over the ducking non-striker. Long-on had no chance
flat and quick again, a touch shorter now, and he rocks back to pull between deep square leg and deep midwicket
down the track, and Hooda fires it into his pads. Too quick for him to connect with the flick
full on the pads, flicked to deep midwicket
tossed up outside off, and that's in the perfect slot for Marsh to launch over the cover boundary. Poor start to the over
bang. It's a length ball on middle stump and Miller clears his front leg and launches it over wide long-on
back of a length angled across, flayed away to third man
not short enough to pull cleanly and he doesn't time it well, but he hits it in the gap, to the left of long-on
back of a length on leg stump, whipped away to deep midwicket
length ball wide of off stump, slapped to sweeper cover
back of a length on middle and off, worked to midwicket off the back foot
this time it's a short slower ball along that tight line just outside off. Very hard to hit, and Miller can't connect with the pull
slower ball outside off, slips under Miller's bat as he shuffles down the track and goes for the big hit through the covers
shortish slower ball on off stump. Through his pull too quickly, bottom-edges towards short midwicket
short ball, pulled away down to deep backward square leg
back of a length on off stump, skids on and hits him on the back thigh as he misses the pull
back of a length, angling in towards off stump, tucked away towards short midwicket
floated up outside off, driven to sweeper cover

down the track comes Marsh, and that's his fifty. It's very full, near his feet, and he's only allowed a short bat-swing at it, but he hits it so cleanly it easily clears the straight boundary, to long-on's right
shoprt and wide, cracked away past point, and this time Morris manages to cut it off with the dive after sprinting from sweeper cover
down the track, whipped to deep midwicket
tossed up on off stump, and Marsh clears his front leg and swings through the line, with the turn and clears the boundary between deep midwicket and long-on
fired down the leg side, paddled towards long leg
angled into the pads, flicked to deep midwicket
fuller now, on off stump, pushed to long-off

length ball, skids on towards off stump as Miller makes room to cut. Punches it towards short cover, where Nair dives to his right to make a brilliant save, and flicks it quickly to the keeper to make Miller decide against the single
back of a length on off stump, and he waits on it to pull-whip it to deep midwicket
back of a length on off stump, shuffles across and works it through square leg
full-toss down the leg side, swept to the left of deep square leg
floated across the left-hander, nice and full, driven to sweeper cover
goes for the slog-sweep now and he's holed out to deep midwicket. Just a bit of turn and bounce from middle and leg and it produces the top edge
looks for the reverse sweep from leg stump, hits it straight to cover point. Didn't quite middle it either
rubbish short ball wide outside off, but it's only a single because sweeper cover exists for balls like that
short ball and Marsh jumps deep in his crease and pulls it witheringly to the straight midwicket boundary
a bit of turn here from leg and middle. It was flat, and Maxwell was looking to turn it into the leg side, but held himself and played it with a relatively full face towards mid-off
tossed up outside off, left alone
lbw appeal from Tambe as Marsh misreads a googly and is hit on the pad, rocking back onto the back foot, but it pitched outside leg stump

tossed up on off stump, and that is brutal from Marsh, a full, free swing of the bat and Maxwell has to duck his head in a hurry at the non-striker's end. Long-off was on the rope but he had no chance of stopping it, running to his left
full on leg stump, clipped to deep midwicket
googly, but it's short and Marsh rocks back to pull from outside off stump to deep midwicket
tossed up outside off, and Maxwell presses forward to defend towards the bowler
down the track now, whips this leg-stump ball to deep midwicket
short and wide, cut away crisply and Morris, sliding across to his right after running round from sweeper cover, could only push it into the boundary rope
slowish ball, angled across towards off stump. Marsh defends it back to the bowler

short outside off, and that's a convoluted way for a bad ball to get a wicket. It stopped on the pitch a bit, and Marsh, shaping to cut, ended up flat-batting it back to Tewatia, who fielded it and turned around in a flash to flick the ball at the stumps, too quick for Vijay, who had backed up too far, to return to his crease.
back of a length outside off, slides with the angle, punched to deep extra cover
slower ball on off stump, and Vijay clears his front leg and swipes it over the straight midwicket boundary. Lovely clean swing of the bat for a shot that can be described as a slog
back of a length, straightens a touch towards off stump, cramps Marsh for room. Jams down on the ball to poke it square on the off side
back of a length, angling across, a bit of extra bounce to beat Marsh's attempted cut
back of a length outside off, dabbed to short third man
length ball outside off, enough width for Marsh to crack it away resoundingly, but straight to cover point
length ball on a fourth-stump line, punched towards mid-off
back of a length outside off, dabbed away to the right of backward point, where it's Hooda's turn to misfield
shot! That's full and angled across and he threads it through the gap between cover point and short cover
a bit of air on off stump, and Nair has dropped a fairly simple catch, diving forward at deep midwicket as Vijay fails to get the requisite elevation on a slog-sweep
full on leg stump, clipped away to deep midwicket
length ball on off stump, punched to mid-on off the back foot
length ball on middle and off, tucked away through midwicket
length ball, angling in towards off stump, tucked off the pads towards deep backward square leg
slower short ball, sits up nicely for Marsh to swivel and pull - it was only a flick of his wrists, really - to the right of the short fine leg fielder
length ball on a fourth-stump line, pushed towards mid-off, lot of bottom hand in that shot
length ball on off stump. Vijay shuffles across, looking to flick, and plays around it. Off the pad and runs into the leg side
shot! Beautifully done by Vijay, who comes down the track, doesn't reach the pitch, but simply extends his arms through the stroke and lifts it over the bowler's head and over the boundary
length ball on off stump, angling in. Marsh stays on the back foot and whips it away forward of square leg
fullish, angling in towards off stump, and Marsh flicks it away past short midwicket, to the left of the fielder
back of a length on a fourth-stump line. Marsh goes back and across to defend into the on side
fullish on leg stump, driven wide of mid-on, doesn't quite time it
length ball angled across Vijay, who looks to flick it and plays too early. Leading edge loops over the covers
full on middle and leg, clipped towards midwicket

fullish outside off, checked drive to mid-off. They go for the single, and Smith goes for the keeper's end and hits the stumps direct. Royals are already celebrating, but it's gone to the third umpire. You can see why. Sehwag is stretching but he's well short of the crease. Sharp thinking from Smith, and a brilliant flat throw. Sehwag started running a touch too late, and was watching the fielder as he ran.
length ball outside off, straightens past Vijay's outside edge as he pokes at it. Feet move very late, and he almost stumbles into the shot
length ball on off stump, whipped uppishly but drops short of mid-on, to his right
back of a length on a fourth-stump line, didn't quite come on as well as Sehwag would have liked, and he punches it to short extra cover
shortish outside off, carved away in typically Sehwag-esque fashion, but straight to backward point
back of a length on off stump, blocked back to the bowler
slower ball on a good length outside off, defended into the off side
quick short ball, is through Vijay and over his left shoulder before he can get in position to hook
length ball outside off, and Vijay waves his bat at it to hit it uppishly to the left of the diving short extra cover fielder
full, angling down the leg side. Vijay gets his front pad in the way as he tries to whip it over the leg side
full on off stump, driven to cover
on the pads, languid flick from Vijay can't beat square leg
